sector_model: nonfinancial software; GAAP earnings and FCF after capex with SBC deducted as a cost; net debt from 10-Q balance sheet
thesis: Adobe (Creative Cloud, Document Cloud, Experience Cloud, Semrush) reported Q3 FY26 revenue 6,760M (+12.9%), GAAP net income 1,827M, diluted EPS 4.62, RPO 22.16B, and per a secondary reproduction of the release raised FY26 GAAP EPS targets to 18.12-18.17 with total ARR 27.50B (+11.2%). Close 239.30 on 2026-11-06 (Nasdaq) gives market cap about 93.1B on 389.2M shares: 12.8x TTM GAAP earnings and a TTM FCF yield of 11.4% (9.1% after SBC), with net debt only about 0.7B and 6.8B of buybacks in 9M. The market appears to price AI disruption of creative tools; evidence that growth and margins hold would close the gap.
counterthesis: A low multiple on mid-teens growth may reflect real risk that generative AI erodes creative-seat pricing and moats; ARR growth is about 11% and part of revenue growth is the Semrush acquisition (closed 2026-04-28, 1.87B). SBC is about 2.1B a year, buybacks (6.8B in 9M) are shrinking shares but absorb nearly all FCF, and the CEO is changing on 2026-12-01 with an interim CFO (secondary source). Goodwill is 14.0B vs equity 11.8B and a 70M impairment was booked. The stock fell 4.8% over the last 5 sessions from 251.47 to 239.30. MD&A, legal proceedings, FY2025 10-K and peers are not read.
invalidation: Total ending ARR growth falling below 9% for two quarters; GAAP operating margin falling below 33% (Q3 GAAP operating income 2.35B on 6.76B is about 34.8%); FCF after SBC below 7B annualized; a large goodwill impairment; adverse legal outcome; AI-first products failing to offset seat pressure.
